paraphrase: The Vibhāṣā reports and rejects the view of the Vibhajyavādins that the mind is by nature pure and is defiled by adventitious defilements; for the Sarvāstivāda a defiled mind is not the same as a pure one.
notes: Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Fascicle number uncertain.

paraphrase: The Vibhāṣā sets out the four great masters' explanations of how dharmas existing in all three times are distinguished — by mode of being (Dharmatrāta), characteristic (Ghoṣaka), state (Vasumitra) and relation (Buddhadeva) — and adopts the explanation by state, defined by activity.
notes: Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Fascicle number from memory (T1545, fasc. 77).

paraphrase: The Vibhāṣā tells the story of Mahādeva — a merchant's son of Mathurā who killed his father, an arhat and his mother, became a monk at the Kukkuṭārāma, claimed arhatship and proclaimed the five points in a verse; the assembly divided, the king sided with the majority, and the arhats went to Kashmir.
notes: Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Fascicle number from memory (T1545, fasc. 99). A hostile Sarvāstivāda account of the Mahāsāṃghika side.
